subject: Precommit traffic variance, KV-cache reuse & pricing implications for OrchidAI pilot
messages:
From: Peter Liang <peter@orchidai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope + sample telemetry for Dedicated pilot

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency profiles and the fallback options. We want to move forward with a 6-week pilot on Dedicated for our inference stack (NLP summarization + retrieval-augmented generation). Before we sign the pilot SOW, procurement asked for a short traffic snapshot to anchor the committed capacity and pricing.

Attached are two files: a 72-hour sample of production telemetry (orchid_sample_telemetry.csv) and a short doc with 12 canonical prompts we want to test (orchid_prompt_examples.pdf). A couple quick notes from our side: 
- Peak concurrent sessions observed in the sample: ~620 across our region (US-West).
- Prompt length median: 120 tokens; response length median: 480 tokens (some longer summaries hit ~2.5k tokens).
- Session mix: 60% short Q/A (prompt < 80 tokens), 30% medium (80-250), 10% long-form (>250).
- KV-cache reuse: we estimate ~45% of requests are continuation-of-session where history is reused.
- Typical P95 tail latency requirement: <= 400ms for short Q/A, <= 1.5s for medium/long.

Can your team confirm what inputs you need to produce a committed-capacity recommendation (GPU count / reserved throughput / pricing bands)? Also flag anything in the sample we should annotate differently.

Cheers,
Peter
Head of Infrastructure, OrchidAI

---

(attachment stubs: orchid_sample_telemetry.csv [csv], orchid_prompt_examples.pdf [pdf])

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Peter Liang <peter@orchidai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + sample telemetry for Dedicated pilot

Thanks Peter — this is exactly the kind of data we need, great call. I skimmed the attachments and left a couple inline notes in the Drive link (shared above). To run a defensible committed-capacity recommendation we need a concise set of answers for the items below (if you can paste them into a reply that helps speed things up):

1) Traffic cadence: average qps across business hours + peak 10-minute qps that corresponds to the 620 concurrent sessions figure.
2) Session duration distribution: mean and P95 session duration (seconds) and whether sessions are long-lived websockets or short HTTP requests.
3) Concurrency model: Is concurrency dominated by concurrent requests (many independent calls) or session affinity (long sessions with KV cache reuse)?
4) Retry/backpressure behavior: do you queue/retry client-side? Any burst throttling rules you currently apply?
4b) Acceptable cold-start fallbacks: are you OK letting a small fraction of requests go to a lower-SKU model during burst?
5) Safety margins: what % headroom do you want above observed peaks for the pilot (10%, 25%, custom)?
6) SLO tiers: we need explicit P50/P95/P99 latency SLOs per workload tier (short/medium/long).
7) Billing/contract constraints: target monthly committed spend band (if you have rough ranges it helps us propose pricing bands rather than a single SKU).

Once we have these, Marissa will sketch a GPU-commit recommendation (mix of A100-style reserved nodes + burst pool) and Karthik will validate KV-cache reuse assumptions into session-affinity sizing.

If helpful we can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon to walk through the sample telemetry together.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

(Signature: Monica Patel | Solutions | redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192)

From: Peter Liang <peter@orchidai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidai.com
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + sample telemetry for Dedicated pilot

Monica — thanks, quick answers below (pulled from the CSV and engineering notes):

1) Traffic cadence:
- Business hours average: 85 qps (US-West window 09:00-18:00 PT)
- Peak 10-minute qps during the sample: 1,150 qps (this aligns with the 620 concurrent sessions; many short Q/A are bursty during marketing emails).

2) Session duration:
- Mean session duration: 18s
- P95 session duration: 87s
- Sessions are short HTTP requests (no long-lived websockets at the moment).

3) Concurrency model:
- Concurrency is mostly independent requests (we open many short requests), but ~45% are continuation requests that include the last-turn KV context (we attach a conversation id). We do not pin sessions to specific machines.

4) Retry/backpressure:
- Client retries up to 2x with exponential backoff; most burst losses are handled by client queueing. We do not currently surface backpressure to users directly.
- Cold-start fallbacks: we can tolerate up to ~3% of requests served by a lower-SKU if it preserves correctness (i.e., smaller model for brief misses).

5) Safety margins: we want 20% headroom for the pilot.

6) SLO tiers:
- Short Q/A: P95 <= 350ms; P99 <= 600ms
- Medium: P95 <= 900ms; P99 <= 1.8s
- Long-form: P95 <= 1.6s; P99 <= 3.5s

7) Budget: procurement prefers committing to a $25k-$50k monthly band for the pilot; we can scale up if the pilot hits success metrics.

Let us know if you need sample traces (we can pull 1-min trace with latency buckets). Happy to hop on the call tomorrow at 2pm PT.

—Peter

(attachment stubs: orchid_sample_telemetry.csv — updated with 1-min traces [csv])

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot scope + sample telemetry for Dedicated pilot — quick sizing ask

Forwarding Orchid's answers (below). Key asks for the sizing calc:
- They are mostly short HTTP requests with notable bursts: 1,150 qps peak (10-min) and 620 concurrent session-equivalent.
- 45% KV-cache reuse (continuations) but no affinity; that maps nicely to our prefix/KV cache savings if we can route consistently.
- P95 targets are tight for short Q/A (<=350ms) which suggests a lower-latency SKU or aggressive batching config.
- Budget target for pilot: $25k-$50k/month — we will need a tiered proposal (committed baseline + burst hours).

Marissa: can you sketch two options: A) conservative commit to meet P95 with 25% headroom (higher baseline, smaller burst pool), B) lean commit (meet avg with 40% burst buffer) and show cost delta.
Karthik: please confirm how 45% KV reuse maps to effective token reduction in our sizing model (I think ~30% token-savings once you account for partial-history reads).

I'll set up a 2pm PT call with Peter for tomorrow and include your preliminary numbers so we can negotiate commit vs burst tradeoffs.

Thanks — Monica

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot scope + sample telemetry for Dedicated pilot — quick sizing ask

All — did a quick first-pass sketch (high level, numbers to validate on call):

Option A (conservative / performance-first):
- Baseline reserved: 6 x rA100-80GB-equivalent nodes (sustains ~800 qps of short Q/A at our low-latency config with continuous batching and per-tenant cache);
- Burst pool (on-demand reserved/spot mix): capacity to scale to peak 1,200 qps for 10-min windows (adds ~2.5 nodes effective);
- Estimated effective token reduction from KV reuse: ~28% (Karthik, please confirm) — I applied that to response token spend.
- Monthly pilot cost estimate (including reserved amortized + burst buffer + infra premium): $48k/month (inside their band, meets P95).

Option B (lean / cost-first):
- Baseline reserved: 3 x rA100-80GB-equivalent nodes (sustains average traffic with caching);
- Burst pool: larger (elastic autoscale) to cover peaks to 1,200 qps — expect slightly higher per-token cost during bursts;
- Estimated effective token reduction from KV reuse: ~22% (assuming some wasted prefix misses in burst windows).
- Monthly pilot cost estimate: $29k/month (falls in lower band), but note we project ~12% of short Q/A may see degraded P95 during simultaneous peak bursts unless we raise baseline or accept a higher tail on bursts.

Next steps: Karthik to confirm KV reduction calc (rough formula: reuse_rate * average_context_fraction_saved * weight) and I'll turn Option A/B into bulletized SOW line items for the 6-week pilot.

—Marissa

(Signature: Marissa Cole | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference)
